name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP)
administering_body: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MoMSME); implemented through Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) as nodal agency, with KVIB and DIC
target_beneficiaries: New/aspiring micro-entrepreneurs, individuals aged 18+, especially in rural and semi-urban areas setting up new manufacturing or service micro-enterprises
support_offered_summary: Credit-linked capital subsidy of approximately 15% to 35% of project cost (varies by category - general/special, urban/rural); project cost ceiling up to Rs 50 lakh for manufacturing and Rs 20 lakh for service units; mandatory Entrepreneurship Development Programme (EDP) training for beneficiaries
eligibility_summary: New units only (no expansion of existing units); age 18+; educational qualification requirements vary by project cost slab; special quota for SC/ST/OBC/minorities/women/ex-servicemen/PwD
data_source: WebSearch aggregated (Cashfree, Sarkari Yojana, HDFC Bank, District Industries Centre Puducherry)
notes: Scheme continuation approved for FY2021-22 to FY2025-26; confirm post-FY26 continuation status via official MSME/KVIC notification when direct fetch is possible. Exact subsidy % bands (urban/rural, general/special category) should be verified against current KVIC guidelines before publishing precise figures.

name: Stand-Up India Scheme
administering_body: Department of Financial Services (DFS), Ministry of Finance; monitored by Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI); implemented via scheduled commercial banks
target_beneficiaries: SC/ST entrepreneurs and women entrepreneurs (at least one SC/ST borrower and one woman borrower per bank branch) setting up greenfield enterprises
support_offered_summary: Composite bank loan (term loan + working capital) between Rs 10 lakh and Rs 1 crore per borrower for greenfield ventures in manufacturing, services, trading or agri-allied sectors; repayment tenure up to 7 years with moratorium up to 18 months; credit guarantee cover via government-backed guarantee mechanism
eligibility_summary: At least 51% shareholding/controlling stake held by an SC/ST or woman entrepreneur; greenfield (first-time) project only; borrower age 18+
data_source: WebSearch aggregated (Legal Service India, IBEF, IIFL, News on Air)
notes: A revamp was announced by the Union Finance Minister in March 2026 reportedly proposing to raise the loan ceiling to Rs 2 crore for women/SC/ST entrepreneurs; as of collection date this appeared to be an announcement/notification-stage change (dated May 5, 2026 per one source) rather than fully confirmed on the official portal - treat revised loan ceiling as PENDING_VERIFICATION until confirmed on standupmitra.in.

name: Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY)
administering_body: Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency (MUDRA) under Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance; loans disbursed via banks, NBFCs, MFIs and RRBs
target_beneficiaries: Non-corporate, non-farm small/micro entrepreneurs and income-generating small business owners across manufacturing, trading and services
support_offered_summary: Collateral-free loans in four tiers: Shishu (up to Rs 50,000), Kishor (above Rs 50,000 up to Rs 5 lakh), Tarun (above Rs 5 lakh up to Rs 10 lakh), and Tarun Plus (above Rs 10 lakh up to Rs 20 lakh, introduced in Union Budget 2024-25 for entrepreneurs who have satisfactorily repaid a previous Tarun loan)
eligibility_summary: Existing or aspiring non-farm micro/small business owners with a viable business plan; Tarun Plus limited to borrowers with a clean repayment record on a prior Tarun loan
data_source: WebSearch aggregated (Sarkari Yojana, Stashfin, Matribhumi Samachar, Yojana Vichar)
notes: Tarun Plus tier confirmed as a 2024-25 Budget addition; loan-tier thresholds are widely and consistently reported across sources, giving reasonable confidence, but interest rates are lender-determined (not fixed by MUDRA) and were not independently verified.

name: Startup India
administering_body: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry
target_beneficiaries: DPIIT-recognized startups (private limited companies, LLPs, registered partnership firms, and per a 2026 framework update, cooperative societies) incorporated within the scheme's eligibility window
support_offered_summary: DPIIT recognition certificate; 3-year income tax holiday under Section 80-IAC (100% profit deduction for 3 consecutive years out of first 10 years); angel tax exemption; 80% patent filing fee rebate; self-certification under select labour/environmental laws; Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups (CGSS) offering guarantees up to Rs 10 crore via SEBI-registered AIFs/lending institutions; SIDBI Fund of Funds 2.0 (Rs 10,000 crore corpus) for equity investment into AIFs; Rs 50 lakh seed grant route reported
eligibility_summary: Entity age typically under 10 years from incorporation (turnover cap reported at Rs 200 crore in a 2026 framework update, Rs 300 crore for a new Deep Tech category with a 20-year recognition window); entity must be working toward innovation/improvement of products, processes or services, or be a scalable business model
data_source: WebSearch aggregated (Legal Service India, myHQ, Vakilsearch, RegisterKaro, Patron Accounting)
notes: 2026 framework details (turnover cap raised to Rs 200 crore, new Deep Tech category with Rs 300 crore cap and 20-year window, cooperative societies made eligible) appear consistently across secondary sources but were not confirmed via a primary DPIIT circular in this session - mark expanded eligibility terms as PENDING_VERIFICATION pending direct portal confirmation.

name: National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC)
administering_body: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE); NSDC is a not-for-profit Public-Private-Partnership company
target_beneficiaries: Youth and workers seeking vocational/skill training, jobseekers, and industry partners requiring skilled workforce; indirectly supports MSME entrepreneurs via skilled labour pipeline and NSDC-affiliated training partners
support_offered_summary: Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) e-learning platform (reported approximately 7,100 courses in 23 languages); NSDC JobX placement/career platform; funding and accreditation support to training partners and sector skill councils; planned 50 Future Skills Centres and 10 NSDC International Academies; organizes IndiaSkills national competitions feeding into WorldSkills
eligibility_summary: Open to Indian youth/jobseekers generally through registered training partners; specific course eligibility (age, education) varies by training partner and scheme
data_source: WebSearch aggregated (NSDC official site, Vajiram & Ravi, BankBazaar, Newkerala)
notes: NSDC underwent a governance overhaul ('NSDC 2.0') from August 2023 with revised board/mandate; the organization's legal name remains National Skill Development Corporation. Course counts and centre-expansion figures are self-reported/press figures and should be treated as approximate.

name: Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE)
administering_body: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MoMSME) and Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI), jointly (Trust structure)
target_beneficiaries: Micro and small enterprises (new and existing) seeking collateral-free credit from member lending institutions (banks, NBFCs, some regional rural/cooperative banks)
support_offered_summary: Credit guarantee cover on collateral-free loans to MSEs, with guarantee coverage commonly cited at 50-85% depending on loan size, borrower category (women/SC-ST/NER etc.) and lending institution type; no collateral or third-party guarantee required for covered loans up to prescribed limits
eligibility_summary: Micro and small enterprises (as defined under the MSME Act, i.e. investment/turnover thresholds) availing eligible credit facilities from a CGTMSE member lending institution
data_source: WebSearch aggregated (CGTMSE official site, Vajiram & Ravi, BankBazaar, Ministry of MSME PDF)
notes: Guarantee coverage percentage is tiered and category-dependent (reported range 50-85%); exact slab-wise percentages were not itemized with full confidence in this session and should be verified against the current CGTMSE scheme document before publishing specific tier figures.

name: PM Vishwakarma Yojana
administering_body: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MoMSME), jointly with Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and other line ministries; delivered via Common Service Centres (CSC)
target_beneficiaries: Traditional artisans and craftspeople (18 identified trades, e.g. carpenters, blacksmiths, goldsmiths, potters, cobblers, tailors, etc.) engaged in hereditary/traditional trades using hand tools
support_offered_summary: Free skill training with stipend of Rs 500/day during training; toolkit incentive e-voucher of Rs 15,000; collateral-free credit support up to Rs 3 lakh in two tranches at 5% concessional interest (Tranche 1 up to Rs 1 lakh/18-month tenure, Tranche 2 up to Rs 2 lakh/30-month tenure, second tranche conditional on satisfactory first-tranche repayment and basic/advanced training completion); digital transaction incentive and marketing support
eligibility_summary: Artisan/craftsperson engaged in one of 18 notified trades, registered via Aadhaar-based biometric authentication at a Common Service Centre, one member per family per trade
data_source: WebSearch aggregated (multiple scheme-tracker sites; original launch Sept 17 2023)
notes: Scheme launched 17 September 2023; benefit structure (Rs 15,000 toolkit, Rs 500/day stipend, Rs 3 lakh total loan at 5%) reported as unchanged into 2026 across sources, but figures should be cross-checked against the official pmvishwakarma.gov.in portal, which could not be directly fetched this session.

name: District Industries Centre (DIC)
administering_body: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MoMSME) at national policy level; individual DICs operationally run by respective State Industries/Commerce Departments (one DIC per district, including all districts of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh)
target_beneficiaries: Aspiring and existing micro, small and cottage/village entrepreneurs at the district level
support_offered_summary: Single-window facilitation at district level: MSME/Udyam registration assistance, project report and financial guidance, raw material and marketing assistance, disbursal/nodal role for schemes such as PMEGP, state industrial incentive processing, technical and managerial guidance, entrepreneurship training coordination
eligibility_summary: Any prospective or existing micro/small entrepreneur within the district; no separate DIC-specific registration fee, generally requires in-person visit (online-only registration not typically available)
data_source: WebSearch aggregated (SMFG India Credit, Paisabazaar, Credlix, Bajaj Finserv, AP district portals)
notes: Treated per task instructions as a single generic entity describing the DIC role/model rather than one row per district (there are 33 districts in Telangana and 26 in Andhra Pradesh, each with its own DIC office). DIC scheme was initiated in 1978 by the Central Government and is implemented identically in principle across all TG and AP districts, though functionally each district's DIC is administered by the respective state government's Industries & Commerce Department; district-level contact points differ but the mandate, services and eligibility described here apply uniformly in both states.

name: T-IDEA (Telangana Industrial Development and Entrepreneurship Advancement)
administering_body: Industries and Commerce Department, Government of Telangana (incentive claims processed via TS-iPASS/Mee Seva and TGIIC-linked industrial areas)
target_beneficiaries: Micro, small, medium, large and mega manufacturing/service enterprises setting up or expanding in Telangana
support_offered_summary: Capital investment subsidy (reported approximately 15% of eligible investment, capped around Rs 20 lakh for MSEs per one source); 100% SGST reimbursement for 5 years for Micro & Small Enterprises; interest subsidy ('Pavala Vaddi') reported up to 9% p.a. on term loans for 5 years; stamp duty exemption/reimbursement on land transactions; land cost rebate up to 25% (capped, reported around Rs 10 lakh)
eligibility_summary: New or expanding industrial units registered under the Telangana Industrial Policy Framework (2015 policy book); specific subsidy tier depends on enterprise category (micro/small/medium/large) and investment size
data_source: WebSearch aggregated (KP IAS Academy, TGFPS, Dhruva Industrial Consultants, India SME Forum)
notes: For FY2023-24, 2,239 claims were reportedly approved with incentives totaling Rs 345.98 crore (per secondary source, not independently confirmed). A separate, newer Telangana MSME Policy-2024 (launched Sept 2024) offers different/overlapping subsidy figures (25% capital subsidy up to Rs 30 lakh) for MSMEs - unclear from available sources whether MSME Policy-2024 supersedes T-IDEA rates for MSME-category units or operates alongside it; flagged as a conflict requiring clarification from the Telangana Industries Department before finalizing exact current subsidy percentages.

name: T-PRIDE (Telangana Programme for Rapid Incubation of Dalit Entrepreneurs)
administering_body: Industries and Commerce Department, Government of Telangana
target_beneficiaries: Scheduled Caste (SC), Scheduled Tribe (ST) and Physically Handicapped (PHC) entrepreneurs in Telangana
support_offered_summary: Enhanced subsidies, funding support and incentives (in addition to/on top of T-IDEA-type incentives) targeted at SC/ST/PHC entrepreneurs; preferential allotment of industrial plots in industrial parks/estates for SC/ST/PHC entrepreneurs
eligibility_summary: Entrepreneur must belong to SC, ST, or physically-challenged (PHC) category and be setting up an eligible manufacturing/service enterprise in Telangana
data_source: WebSearch aggregated (KP IAS Academy, MSME Council, Dhruva Industrial Consultants)
notes: Also referenced as 'TS-PRIDE' in some secondary sources; exact current subsidy percentages/quantum for T-PRIDE specifically (distinct from base T-IDEA incentives) were not clearly itemized in available sources and should be verified against the official Telangana Industrial Policy Framework document.

name: TG-iPASS (Telangana State Industrial Project Approval and Self-Certification System; formerly TS-iPASS)
administering_body: Industries and Commerce Department, Government of Telangana, under the TS-iPASS Act 2014 (Act No. 3 of 2014)
target_beneficiaries: All entrepreneurs and enterprises (MSME to large/mega) seeking statutory approvals/clearances to establish or operate industries in Telangana
support_offered_summary: Single-window, time-bound, self-certification-based clearance system; 23 departments and approximately 40 types of approvals brought under one process; clearance timelines ranging from 1 day up to a maximum of 30 days depending on approval complexity; recognized by Government of India as an Ease of Doing Business best practice
eligibility_summary: Any entity setting up or operating an industrial/business enterprise in Telangana requiring statutory departmental clearances (land, power, pollution, factory licence, etc.)
data_source: WebSearch aggregated (IndiaFilings, Wikipedia via search summary, HMDA, Directorate of Town and Country Planning Telangana)
notes: Confirmed rename from 'TS-iPASS' (Telangana State) to 'TG-iPASS' (Telangana) reflecting the state's updated abbreviation convention; both TS-iPASS and TG-iPASS terminology still appear in circulation across government and third-party sites, with ipass.telangana.gov.in now branded as TG-iPASS. Underlying Act (2014) and process remain unchanged.

name: WE-HUB (Women Entrepreneurs Hub)
administering_body: Government of Telangana (established as India's first state-led incubator for women entrepreneurs, announced at Global Entrepreneurship Summit 2017)
target_beneficiaries: Women entrepreneurs at any stage of their entrepreneurial journey, across sectors, rural and urban, irrespective of educational/financial/demographic background
support_offered_summary: Incubation, mentoring, funding facilitation, access to government schemes, corporate/academic collaboration network, and acceleration programmes (e.g. RAMP women-acceleration programme supporting 45 women-led MSMEs across 13 Telangana districts through March 2027); international collaborations (e.g. DEI training programme with Japan's HERALBONY/JICA)
eligibility_summary: Women entrepreneur (proprietor/majority stakeholder) based in or operating in Telangana; no fixed sector restriction
data_source: WebSearch aggregated (WE-HUB official site, KP IAS Academy, News on Air)
notes: Also hosts the NITI Aayog Women Entrepreneurship Platform's first state chapter (launched Oct 2024). Continues to operate under the same name/branding as of mid-2026; no rename identified.

name: TASK (Telangana Academy for Skill and Knowledge)
administering_body: Government of Telangana, Information Technology, Electronics and Communications Department (IT&EC)
target_beneficiaries: College students and young graduates in Telangana seeking employability/technical skilling; also supports entrepreneurship among youth
support_offered_summary: Technology skilling programmes delivered in partnership with industry (Oracle, Infosys, Google, IBM, Microsoft, Autodesk, SAP) and academia (IIIT-Hyderabad, NIT Warangal, IIT Hyderabad, BITS Pilani); focus on Personal Impact Skills, Organization Impact Skills and Technical Skills; collaboration platform linking Government, Academia and Industry for skilling, research and entrepreneurship
eligibility_summary: Primarily students/graduates of Telangana engineering and degree colleges; specific programme eligibility varies by partner course
data_source: WebSearch aggregated (TASK official site, Telangana Web Directory, engineering college portals)
notes: Established 2014, continues to operate under the same name as of collection date; no rename identified. Entrepreneurship role is secondary to its primary employability-skilling mandate.

name: TGIIC (Telangana Industrial Infrastructure Corporation; formerly TSIIC)
administering_body: Government of Telangana, Industries and Commerce Department (state-owned corporation)
target_beneficiaries: Industrial and MSME units, IT/SEZ/biotech/textile park occupants requiring developed industrial land/infrastructure in Telangana
support_offered_summary: Development and allotment of industrial parks/estates and plots (ranging roughly 15 to 2,500 acres), including internal roads, power, water supply, drainage, and environmental clearance facilitation for Industrial Areas, SEZs, IT Parks, Biotech Parks and Textile & Apparel Parks
eligibility_summary: Industrial/MSME units seeking land allotment or infrastructure access within TGIIC-developed industrial parks/estates in Telangana
data_source: WebSearch aggregated (TGIIC official site, Telangana Web Directory, The South First, Wikipedia via search summary)
notes: Confirmed rename from TSIIC (Telangana State Industrial Infrastructure Corporation) to TGIIC (Telangana Industrial Infrastructure Corporation); both tsiic.telangana.gov.in and tgiic.telangana.gov.in domains were found active in search results, with tgiic.telangana.gov.in appearing as the current primary site. TGIIC was listed on NSE as a High Value Debt Listed Entity (HVDLE) on 12 December 2024. A political dispute (opposition allegation re: converting TGIIC into a public limited company / land mortgage, reported 2025) was noted in news sources but not independently verified - flagged as a developing/contested matter, not a confirmed factual change to the corporation's core mandate.

name: Telangana MSME Policy 2024
administering_body: Industries and Commerce Department, Government of Telangana (launched by CM A. Revanth Reddy)
target_beneficiaries: New and existing MSMEs across Telangana, with special provisions for SC/ST entrepreneurs and women entrepreneurs
support_offered_summary: Rs 4,000 crore planned outlay over 5 years; land cost subsidy reported at 50% for SC/ST entrepreneurs and 25% for other MSMEs (with an additional 20% subsidy layer reported for women entrepreneurs); capital investment subsidy of 25% on fixed capital investment (land, building, plant and machinery) capped at Rs 30 lakh; 100% SGST reimbursement for first 5 years from commercial production; power tariff subsidy of Rs 1/unit for first 5 years; Rs 100 crore 'Yantram Fund' for MSME technology adoption; 5 of 10 new industrial parks reserved for MSMEs (one for women-owned units, one for startups)
eligibility_summary: New and existing MSME units in Telangana as defined under the MSME Act; enhanced subsidy tiers apply to SC/ST and women-owned enterprises specifically
data_source: WebSearch aggregated (Telangana State Portal, Business Standard, BankExamsToday, News on Air)
notes: Launched 18 September 2024, targeting 25,000 new MSMEs over 5 years. Subsidy terms (e.g. 25% capital subsidy capped at Rs 30 lakh) appear to differ from the older T-IDEA scheme's cited terms (15% capped at Rs 20 lakh) - relationship between the two (supersession vs. parallel operation) is PENDING_VERIFICATION; recommend checking the official PDF at telangana.gov.in directly once fetch access is available.

name: APIIC (Andhra Pradesh Industrial Infrastructure Corporation Limited)
administering_body: Government of Andhra Pradesh, Department of Industries (state-owned corporation, established 1973)
target_beneficiaries: Industrial and MSME units, IT/SEZ park occupants requiring developed industrial land/infrastructure in Andhra Pradesh
support_offered_summary: Development, allotment and management of industrial parks/estates, plots, sheds and related infrastructure (roads, power, water, drainage) across Andhra Pradesh; land monetization/leasing for industrial development
eligibility_summary: Industrial/MSME units seeking land allotment or infrastructure access within APIIC-developed industrial parks/estates in Andhra Pradesh
data_source: WebSearch aggregated (APIIC official site, Wikipedia via search summary, Business Standard, Dhruva Industrial Consultants)
notes: One older source (APIIC's own objectives page) states the corporation 'shall be named' Corporation for Industrial Infrastructure in Andhra Pradesh (CIAP) and registered as a joint stock company - this appears to reference a legal/incorporation provision rather than a completed public rename, since the entity continues to be branded and referred to as APIIC across current government sources (2022-2025). Treat the CIAP designation as PENDING_VERIFICATION rather than a confirmed current rename.

name: AP Innovation Society (APIS) / Startup AP
administering_body: Government of Andhra Pradesh, Department of Information Technology, Electronics and Communications (implements the AP Innovation & Startup Policy)
target_beneficiaries: Startup founders and innovation-stage entrepreneurs in Andhra Pradesh, including women, SC/ST, BC and minority founders
support_offered_summary: Operates 4 Technology Business Incubators and 1 Technology Business Accelerator across the state; 4-month acceleration training programme; mentorship, co-working space access, accounting assistance, IP/patent filing support; tiered grants reportedly up to Rs 20 lakh in phased support for women/SC/ST/BC/minority founders, scaling grants up to Rs 15 lakh, and prototype/PoC grants of Rs 2 lakh; 'AP Startup One' single-window portal for registration, grant application and status tracking
eligibility_summary: Startup/entrepreneur recognized or registering under the AP Innovation & Startup Policy 4.0 (2024-29), operating in or relocating to Andhra Pradesh
data_source: WebSearch aggregated (APIS official site, IndiaFilings, StartupIndia state policy page, StartupFlora, StartupGrantsIndia)
notes: Governed by AP Innovation & Startup Policy 4.0 (2024-2029); grant amounts (Rs 20 lakh/15 lakh/2 lakh tiers) are drawn from secondary aggregator sites and should be cross-verified against the official APIS policy document before being treated as final figures.

name: Andhra Pradesh MSME and Entrepreneurship Development Policy 4.0 (2024-2029)
administering_body: Department of Industries, Government of Andhra Pradesh
target_beneficiaries: New and existing Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises in Andhra Pradesh, with enhanced provisions for women, BC, SC, ST and specially-abled entrepreneurs
support_offered_summary: Capital subsidy of 25% of Fixed Capital Investment (FCI), capped at Rs 25 lakh (micro), Rs 1.5 crore (small) and Rs 7 crore (medium) enterprises; enhanced capital subsidy up to 35% of FCI for women, BC, SC, ST and specially-abled entrepreneurs; employment-generation incentive of 8-10% of FCI disbursed over 5-7 years; 100% SGST reimbursement for 5 years (capped at 5% of annual turnover); overall incentive cap of 75% of FCI across all incentive components combined; policy valid for 5 years from notification
eligibility_summary: New or existing MSME unit in Andhra Pradesh as defined under the MSME Act; enhanced subsidy tier requires entrepreneur to belong to a specified category (woman/BC/SC/ST/specially-abled)
data_source: WebSearch aggregated (KIP Financial Consultancy, Unique Group, eUdyamAadhar)
notes: Policy branded '4.0' indicating it is the fourth iteration of AP's MSME policy series, launched under the current (Naidu-led) state government. Detailed subsidy figures sourced from consultancy secondary summaries rather than a directly fetched official notification - recommend confirming exact caps against the official Department of Industries G.O./policy PDF.
